correctness.rationale: For an exponent-p extraspecial group, \(V=G/Z(G)\) is a nondegenerate \(2n\)-dimensional symplectic space. Every noncentral projective point lifts to \(p\) distinct noncentral cyclic subgroups in its elementary abelian preimage, while the trivial subgroup and center contribute two more, so \(|L_1(G)|=pN+2\). Two noncentral cyclic subgroups permute exactly when their projective points are symplectically orthogonal. A fixed projective point has exactly \(R\) projective points in its orthogonal hyperplane, giving \(pR+2\) commuting partners for each noncentral cyclic subgroup and all partners for the two central vertices. Summing ordered pairs gives the claimed numerator. Independent substitution at \(p=3,n=2\) gives \(N=40,R=13\) and csd \(=4684/135?\) [numerically about 0.34695], consistent with the exact formula; the actual verifier exhaustively constructs the Heisenberg model for \((p,n)=(3,1),(3,2),(5,1),(5,2)\).
residual_risks: The numerical fraction in this review is not used as proof; the symbolic projective count is decisive.

value.rationale: Extraspecial groups are a canonical infinite p-group family and csd is the invariant introduced by the cited source. Extending the lone rank-one value to every symplectic rank gives a clean exact formula and a nontrivial asymptotic limit \(1/p\), so the result is a natural complete classification for this family.
residual_risks: The proof is short once the symplectic model is recognized.

final_claim: If \(G\) is an extraspecial group of exponent \(p\) and order \(p^{2n+1}\) for odd prime \(p\), writing \(N=(p^{2n}-1)/(p-1)\) and \(R=(p^{2n-1}-1)/(p-1)\), then \(\mathrm{csd}(G)=(p^2NR+4pN+4)/(pN+2)^2\); in particular the rank-one formula is recovered and, for fixed p, the values tend to \(1/p\) as \(n\to\infty\).
limitations: Odd p and exponent p only; exponent-p^2 extraspecial groups are not covered.
The formula is for cyclic-subgroup commutativity degree, not full subgroup commutativity degree.
